classification.difficultyReason: Model compound growth symbolically and determine whole-year thresholds by calculator trials and logarithms.

content.prompt: A principal $P$ dollars is invested at 7% per annum compound interest. Let $A_n$ be the total amount at the end of $n$ years.

answer.worked:
The first term is $a=1.07P$ and the common ratio is $r=1.07$.
$$\begin{align*}A_n&=ar^{n-1}\\A_n&=(1.07P)(1.07)^{n-1}\\A_n&=P(1.07)^n\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use trial-and-error on the calculator to find how many full years it will take for the amount to double, and how many years it will take for it to exceed ten times the original principal.

answer.short: 11 years to double; 35 years to exceed ten times the original principal.
answer.worked:
To double, require $A_n\ge2P$, so $(1.07)^n\ge2$. Calculator trials give
$$\begin{align*}(1.07)^{10}&\approx1.9672<2\\(1.07)^{11}&\approx2.1049>2\end{align*}$$
The first full year is 11.

To exceed ten times the principal, require $A_n>10P$, so $(1.07)^n>10$. Calculator trials give
$$\begin{align*}(1.07)^{34}&\approx9.9781<10\\(1.07)^{35}&\approx10.6766>10\end{align*}$$
The first full year is 35.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Use logarithms to confirm your answer.

answer.short: Doubling requires $n\ge\log_{1.07}2\approx10.24$, giving 11 years. Exceeding ten times the principal requires $n>\log_{1.07}10\approx34.03$, giving 35 years.
answer.worked:
For doubling:
$$\begin{align*}(1.07)^n&\ge2\\n&\ge\log_{1.07}2\\\log_{1.07}2&\approx10.24\end{align*}$$
The least whole number of years is 11.

For exceeding ten times the principal:
$$\begin{align*}(1.07)^n&>10\\n&>\log_{1.07}10\\\log_{1.07}10&\approx34.03\end{align*}$$
The least whole number of years is 35.
